query: Two teams opened incidents twenty minutes apart — billing_facts USD amounts fell 31% and usage_rollup spend came in 28% under forecast. Are these the same problem?
expected_behavior: Scopes the upstream ancestors of BOTH symptoms rather than investigating one and stopping
Intersects the ancestor sets to find assets upstream of both
Discards a shared ancestor that carries no fault of its own — being a common dependency is not evidence of being the broken one
Identifies currency_rates as the shared cause, and reports its own freshness lag as the evidence
Verifies a lineage path from currency_rates to EACH symptom separately, rather than asserting the second by association with the first
States the grounding at the weakest rung across those proofs, because a group claim cannot be better grounded than its worst link
Names any incident it cannot prove the shared cause reaches, instead of folding it into the group
Files one dossier for the shared cause rather than one per symptom
